[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

I've reviewed the Seller's package against our playbook. It departs from our positions on nearly every material point. Below are the issues, my reasoning, and recommendations. 

**Important caveat up front:** Several of these Seller positions are asserted as "agreed," "settled," or "adequate." None of them are agreed from our side, and nothing in these documents triggers any of our fallbacks. Fallbacks require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft — I have no record of any such authority. The fact that a Seller number *happens* to match one of our fallback figures does not clear it.

---

## Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.

**Playbook:** Starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / 4,800,000 figure is a *conditional fallback* usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority. None has been given.

**Reasoning:** This is the trap to watch. The Seller's cap coincidentally equals our authorised fallback number — but we are not cleared to accept it. Accepting it now would skip both our opening position and the authority gate. **Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** Do not treat the match as pre-cleared.

---

## Thresholds (Clause 12.2)

**Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **only the excess above the basket** recoverable.

**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable **from the first dollar** once exceeded.

**Reasoning:** Three separate departures, all adverse. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and the "excess only" (deductible) structure contradicts our first-dollar (tipping-basket) requirement. **Reject all three.**

---

## Time Limits (Clause 12.3 / 13)

**Seller:** 18 months for general claims; and a sweeper that any limitation applies to *all* claims unless expressly stated.

**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none given). Fundamental/Title must sit in a separate regime (≥6 years).

**Reasoning:** Again, 18 months matches our fallback but is not cleared — **push to 24 months.** The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" sweeper is dangerous: it is a hidden general-regime override designed to drag Fundamental/Title/Tax into the short period. **Reject the sweeper; require express carve-outs.**

---

## Fundamental / Title Regime

**Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the *same* caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."

**Playbook:** Separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to surrender title protection. This would cap title claims at 20% and cut them to 18 months — unacceptable. **Reject; insist on a standalone fundamental regime.**

---

## Limitations / Exclusive Remedy / Non-Reliance (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Seller:** All limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature."

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

**Reasoning:** "All Claims of any nature" would sweep in fraud. This is a non-negotiable. **Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across every limitation.** Also note DD-006 (incident) should not be caught by non-reliance where it depends on facts the Seller controls.

---

## Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1, 1.2)

**Seller:** General deemed disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.

**Playbook:** Require specific, fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Reasoning:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 are exactly the blanket deemed-disclosure constructs we reject — they would let the Seller disclose a known problem by burying it anywhere in the data room. **Require specific disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the fact, matter and extent.** Note §1.4 also disclaims that anything is "legally required" — fine as a reservation, but it does not convert blanket disclosure into fair disclosure.

---

## Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3)

**Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Reasoning:** This is a blanket, constructive-knowledge ("discoverable") bar — worse than actual knowledge, and expressly tied to the deemed-disclosure trick above. **Delete.** If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be actual knowledge of named individuals and must never touch title, capacity, fraud or the Ironquay/other specific indemnities.

---

## Bluefen Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3)

**Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours" and consent treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** as at the letter date.

**Playbook:** Require effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer (~30% of revenue, ~AUD 3.6m).

**Reasoning:** This is a material customer. "Consent-on-delivery" ignores that clause 11.2/11.3 impose *conditions* — delivery of a consent letter doesn't prove the conditions are met. The Disclosure Letter itself confirms neither exists yet. **Make effective consent plus satisfaction-of-conditions evidence a Completion condition.**

---

## Riverlark (Clause 2 / 7)

**Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 facility addressed by a release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter §3: not repaid, no discharge included.

**Playbook:** Require current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

**Reasoning:** A bare post-Completion release leaves us owning a company with live bank security and no guaranteed discharge. **Require direct payout from completion funds and effective release at Completion.** If any release genuinely must follow Completion, it needs an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval (not given). This also interacts with debt-free/cash-free pricing.

---

## Employee Bonuses (Funds Flow / DD-005)

**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller," **not itemised in the funds flow.** Disclosure §5: on-costs (payroll tax, super) not addressed.

**Playbook:** The AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Reasoning:** "Not separately itemised" is the silent-exclusion risk we guard against. If these are Completion-triggered and continued-employment bonuses, the economic burden and on-costs must not fall on us by omission. **Require a specific line item or express seller funding, including on-costs.** Confirm who bears payroll tax/super.

---

## Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)

**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." AUD 180,000 cited.

**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

**Reasoning:** Disclosure §4 confirms transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee, and there's **no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment** in the data room. The risk isn't just the AUD 180,000 — it's whether we actually get the IP/materials. The AUD 180,000 is a Seller/internal figure, not bank-verified. **Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of the assignment/materials transfer, preserve the SOW3 cure, and don't accept AUD 180,000 as settled quantum.**

---

## Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006 / Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)

**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material." Disclosure §6: download link sent to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether anyone accessed it, scope, or notification duty.

**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

**Reasoning:** The Seller's characterisation ("not material") is an assertion, not a finding — and we equally should not assume it *is* a breach. The correct posture is process, not conclusion. **Require log/evidence preservation, continued investigation, and information undertakings; keep remedies open pending facts.** Resist any non-reliance/knowledge bar attaching to this item given facts sit with the Seller.

---

## Sandbar Renewals (Supplier renewals)

**Seller:** Three renewals AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure §8: silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Reasoning:** We should neither accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor automatically treat these as Debt. **Request the contracts to assess terminability/accrual** and decide on treatment; don't concede either way yet.

---

## Title (Disclosure §10 / DD-012)

**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

**Playbook:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied *internal* source, not independent proof.

**Reasoning:** A company's own register is self-serving. **Require independent verification** of ownership, encumbrances and authority, and keep title in the fundamental regime (see above). The Disclosure Letter itself notes we haven't completed our own verification — so we must.

---

## Tax / IP (said to be "settled under the general regime")

**Seller:** Considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime.

**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Keep Tax/IP categories separate from the general regime.

**Reasoning:** "Settled" is an assertion, not an agreement — and folding Tax/IP into the general regime is another hidden override (short period, low cap). **Reject "settled"; keep Tax and IP as separate open categories.**

---

## Other flagged items (watch, not concede)

- **Office lease (§7):** notification obligation noted; Seller says not a consent condition. Confirm independently whether notice/consent affects Completion.
- **Mossvale (§9):** assignment restriction; Seller says not triggered by share sale. Verify against the actual clause — don't rely on the Seller's reading.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

1. **Cap:** Reject 20%/4.8m; demand 25%/6.0m. The match to our fallback is *not* clearance.
2. **Thresholds:** Reject 25k/250k/excess-only; demand 5k de minimis, 50k first-dollar basket.
3. **Time limits:** Reject 18 months and the "applies to all Claims" sweeper; demand 24 months and express carve-outs.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** Reject merger into the general regime; insist on separate 100% / ≥6-year regime outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** Insert non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
6. **Disclosure:** Reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure; require specific, fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete the blanket/constructive-knowledge bar; any qualifier limited to named persons' actual knowledge, never touching title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** Make effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied a Completion condition; reject reasonable-endeavours/consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** Direct payout from completion funds + effective release at Completion; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 + on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; no silent exclusion.
11. **Ironquay:** Broaden indemnity (cover failed assignment/materials), preserve SOW3 cure; don't accept 180k as settled.
12. **DD-006:** Preservation, investigation and update obligations; no concession of breach/no-breach; keep remedies open.
13. **Sandbar:** Obtain contracts and assess; no automatic Debt/price deduction either way.
14. **Title:** Require independent verification; DD-012 register is not independent proof.
15. **Tax/IP:** Treat as open and separate; reject "settled under the general regime."

**Authority note for the team:** Items 1 and 3 involve numbers matching our authorised fallbacks. Please confirm with Amelia Frost whether she wishes to open at our starting positions (my recommendation) — we have **no written authority on file** to accept the 20% cap or the 18-month period, so I've treated both as push-backs.

Would you like me to turn this into a mark-up or an issues list for the Seller?
